content.text: This is the known `ar`/`ranlib` failure caused by the `libslic3r_gui` static library growing past 4 GiB — Apple's `ar` tool can't handle archives that large. I recorded the fix for this exact problem before, so let me pull it up.

description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does

Confirmed — it's exactly the same failure as before: `Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF)` in Apple's `ar`, hit while building `liblibslic3r_gui.a` in `RelWithDebInfo`. That static library has grown past the 4 GiB limit Apple's `ar`/`ranlib` can handle (it uses 32-bit offsets internally), so archiving fails even though the actual link would work fine.

## Why the build fails

`./build_release_macos.sh -s -x -b -c RelWithDebInfo` builds the `libslic3r_gui` static library in `RelWithDebInfo` mode. The project's root `CMakeLists.txt` (around line 544–548) deliberately downgrades `RelWithDebInfo` from `-O2` to `-O0` so debugging is easier, which means object files carry very little optimization and a lot of debug info — that's what's pushing the combined archive over 4 GiB. Apple's stock `ar` (from Xcode's toolchain) asserts once a member's offset inside the archive exceeds `0xFFFFFFFF` (4 GiB), so `ar qc`/`ranlib` crash instead of producing the file.

This isn't a code regression — it's a toolchain limit that the archive size just crossed on this branch (`jusprin-newui`).

## The fix

LLVM's `ar`/`ranlib` (already installed via Homebrew at `/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/`) don't have this limit and can write archives past 4 GiB. Setting `-DCMAKE_AR=...` on an *existing* build directory won't work — CMake's generated `CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets `CMAKE_AR` as a normal variable that shadows the cache value, so it's silently ignored. There are two real options:

1. **One-time manual relink** (fast, no reconfigure): dump the exact `ar`/`ranlib` commands Ninja would run for this target, swap the binaries to `llvm-ar`/`llvm-ranlib` on just the `liblibslic3r_gui.a` line, and run it directly so this build finishes.
2. **Lasting fix**: reconfigure the build from scratch with `llvm-ar`/`llvm-ranlib` set at cache-creation time (before `CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` exists), or reduce debug info in `RelWithDebInfo` so the archive shrinks back under 4 GiB.

I checked this directly against CMake's own bundled modules (not guessing) rather than trusting the earlier memory note blindly. Here's what's actually going on and what it takes.

## Why a normal reconfigure doesn't pick up `CMAKE_AR`

CMake only auto-detects the archiver (`ar`) and `ranlib` once per build directory, the first time it determines the C/C++ compiler. The result gets written into a generated file — in this project, `build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` (and the matching `CMakeCCompiler.cmake` for C). That file hardcodes `CMAKE_AR` and `CMAKE_RANLIB` as literal paths, and it also writes `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID_RUN 1` into itself. On every later `cmake ..` reconfigure, CMake loads that file first, sees `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID_RUN` already set to 1, and skips compiler/archiver detection entirely — so passing `-DCMAKE_AR=...` on a reconfigure of the existing `build/arm64` directory is silently ignored. This matches what I noted from an earlier session, and I've now confirmed the exact mechanism by reading CMake 3.29's `CMakeDetermineCXXCompiler.cmake` and the `.cmake.in` template it fills in.

## What it actually takes

You need CMake to forget it already detected the compiler, so it redoes that step and bakes in the new `ar`/`ranlib` paths. There are two ways to get there:

**Option A — targeted reset (cheaper, expected to only relink, not fully rebuild):**
Delete just the compiler-detection cache files for this build directory, then reconfigure with the LLVM archiver:

```bash
rm -rf /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake \
       /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCCompiler.cmake \
       /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_CXX.bin \
       /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_C.bin \
       /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdC \
       /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdCXX
cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64
cmake . -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

Since `ar`/`ranlib` only matter for the final "package these `.o` files into a `.a`" step (not for compiling each `.cpp`), and all the actual compiler flags/paths stay the same, this should only cause Ninja to re-run the archive-link steps, not recompile the ~285 translation units in `libslic3r_gui`. That's my expectation based on how CMake and Ninja's rebuild rules work — I haven't run it end-to-end yet, so treat it as likely rather than certain until we watch it happen.

**Option B — full clean reconfigure (guaranteed correct, expensive):**
Delete the whole `build/arm64` directory and let `build_release_macos.sh` recreate it from scratch. This is unambiguous but means recompiling the entire slicer target at `-O0` with full debug info, which on this codebase is a long build (likely well over an hour).

Either way, `build_release_macos.sh` itself doesn't expose an `-DCMAKE_AR=...` flag today, so this has to be done as a one-off manual `cmake` invocation (like above) rather than through the script's normal flags. If you want this to survive future `./build_release_macos.sh -c RelWithDebInfo` runs without repeating this by hand, the flag would need to be added to the script's `build_slicer()` cmake call at [build_release_macos.sh:198-207](build_release_macos.sh:198).

# macOS build troubleshooting

Recipes for build failures on this fork that are environment/toolchain issues,
not code regressions. Kept separate from `agent-docs/jusprin/` because these
apply to the OrcaSlicer build system generally, not to JusPrin product code.

## `liblibslic3r_gui.a` exceeds 4 GiB: Apple `ar`/`ranlib` assertion

### Symptom

`./build_release_macos.sh -s -x -b -c RelWithDebInfo` (or any RelWithDebInfo
build of the `slicer` target) fails while archiving, not compiling:

```
[36/42] Linking CXX static library src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a
FAILED: [code=1] src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a
Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF), function update_block_invoke, file ArchiveWriter.cpp, line 276.
fatal error: .../usr/bin/ar: fatal error in .../usr/bin/ranlib
```

All `.cpp`/`.mm` files for `libslic3r_gui` compiled fine; only the final
archive step fails.

### Root cause

Apple's stock `ar`/`ranlib` (from the Xcode toolchain) use 32-bit member
offsets internally and assert once an archive crosses 4 GiB
(`0xFFFFFFFF` bytes). `liblibslic3r_gui.a` in `RelWithDebInfo` carries full
debug info at `-O0` — the root `CMakeLists.txt` (around line 544-548)
deliberately rewrites `RelWithDebInfo` from `-O2` to `-O0` for easier
debugging — and as the JusPrin fork has added more GUI code (`Agent/`,
`PrinterSetup/`, `Home/`, `Mcp/`, `Shell/`, `Workspace/`, etc.), the archive
has grown past that limit. This first hit on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-09-13 at
commit `770bd2b0a2`; it will recur, and get worse, as the fork keeps growing.
It is not disk space (plenty was free) and not a code bug — the same source
links fine once a 64-bit-capable archiver is used.

### Fix: use LLVM's `ar`/`ranlib` instead of Apple's

LLVM's archiver (installed via `brew install llvm`, present at
`/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` and `llvm-ranlib`) has no such limit and
accepted a 4,288,175,376-byte archive without complaint.

**The trap:** `-DCMAKE_AR=...` on an *existing* build directory does nothing.
CMake only auto-detects the archiver once, the first time it determines the
C/C++ compiler, and bakes the result into
`build/arm64/CMakeFiles/<cmake-version>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` (and the `C`
equivalent) as a literal `set(CMAKE_AR "...")`. That generated file also sets
`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID_RUN 1`, and every later `cmake ..` reconfigure loads it
first and skips compiler/archiver detection entirely because that variable is
already set — so a `-DCMAKE_AR=` flag on a reconfigure is silently ignored.
(Verified 2026-09-13 by reading CMake 3.29's own
`CMakeDetermineCXXCompiler.cmake` and `CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake.in`.)

To make the override take effect, CMake has to redo compiler detection from
scratch. Two ways to get there:

**Option A — targeted reset (cheaper, not yet verified end-to-end).** Delete
just the compiler-detection cache files, then reconfigure:

```bash
rm -rf build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCCompiler.cmake \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_CXX.bin \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_C.bin \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdC \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdCXX
cd build/arm64
cmake . -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

`ar`/`ranlib` only matter for the final archive step, not for compiling each
`.cpp`, so this is expected to make Ninja only relink static-library targets
rather than recompile every translation unit — but this has not been proven
in practice. Adjust `3.29.0` to match your CMake version
(`build/arm64/CMakeFiles/` has the exact directory name).

**Option B — full clean reconfigure (guaranteed, expensive; this is what was
actually run and verified on 2026-09-13).** Wipe the whole build directory —
it is pure generated output, safe to delete — and reconfigure from nothing:

```bash
rm -rf build/arm64
mkdir -p build/arm64
cd build/arm64
cmake /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin \
  -G "Ninja Multi-Config" \
  -DORCA_TOOLS=ON \
  REDACTED \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.3 \
  -DCMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH="/opt/local:/usr/local:/opt/homebrew" \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar \
  -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local"
cmake --build . --config RelWithDebInfo --target all
```

This pays for a full rebuild of the entire slicer target (every `.cpp`/`.mm`
file, not just `libslic3r_gui`) at `-O0` with full debug info, so budget real
time for it (order of an hour on Apple Silicon).

**Deps-path gotcha, easy to miss:** on this machine, `JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`
is an empty skeleton — no Boost, no TBB, nothing — kept that way to save
disk. The real, already-built dependencies for this fork
(Boost 1.84.0, TBB, OpenSSL, CURL, Freetype, libpng, NLopt, OpenVDB, GMP/MPFR,
OpenCV, JPEG, wxWidgets, etc.) live in the sibling checkout at
`~/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. A fresh
configure that only uses `build_release_macos.sh`'s own computed
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` (JusPrin's own deps dir) fails immediately with `Could
NOT find Boost`. Always include the OrcaSlicer sibling path too, as shown
above — this mirrors the worktree build pattern already used for
`jusprin-newui` worktrees.

### Once fixed

`build/arm64`'s CMake cache now has `llvm-ar`/`llvm-ranlib` and the correct
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` baked in, so ordinary incremental builds — including
`./build_release_macos.sh -s -x -b -c RelWithDebInfo` (`-b` = don't
reconfigure) — keep using them without any special handling. This is
deliberately *not* wired into `build_release_macos.sh` itself: the script has
no flag for a custom archiver or for the sibling deps path, so recreating
`build/arm64` from scratch again means repeating the manual `cmake` steps
above rather than just re-running the script.

Verified 2026-09-13 on `jusprin-newui` at `770bd2b0a2`: full clean rebuild via
Option B completed with exit code 0, zero `error:` lines in the build log,
final `liblibslic3r_gui.a` at 4,288,175,376 bytes (past the 4 GiB point that
broke Apple's `ar`), confirmed a valid `current ar archive` via `file`, and
`OrcaSlicer.app`'s binary linked successfully.
